The second objective explicitly frames multiplication as repeated addition, so proficiency in addition substantively supports success in this multiplication objective, justifying a same-rank developmental direction from addition to the repeated-addition multiplication skill. Shared grade/theme/sub-theme and token overlap alone would not suffice, but the conceptual dependency on addition is source-backed in the objective text.

judgment.rationale: First objective is identifying 2D shapes (square, rectangle, circle) under Topic '2. Two dimensional shapes'; second is distinguishing 3D shapes (cuboids vs cubes) under Topic '1. Three dimensional shapes'. Both sit within the same Primary One Sub-Theme 'Shapes' and Theme 'Mensuration and Geometry' and are complementary shape-recognition/discrimination skills, giving substantive conceptual coherence. However they address different shape dimensions and distinct topics, and share the same grade rank (0) with no substantive evidence that mastering 2D identification supports success in distinguishing specific 3D solids, so no directional buildsTowards is warranted. relatesTo captures the meaningful shape-domain reinforcement without asserting dependency.

judgment.rationale: The second objective (identify and read correctly the numbers 1-99, under Number and Numeration / Whole Numbers 1-99) develops number recognition and reading across the 1-99 range. The first objective (add 2-digit whole numbers with sum not greater than 40 without exchanging, under Basic Operations / Addition) requires operating on two-digit numbers, which presupposes the ability to identify and read such numbers. Proficiency in reading/identifying numbers 1-99 substantively supports success in adding two-digit numbers, so the second builds towards the first. Both are PRIMARY ONE (rank 0), so direction rests on this conceptual dependency, not rank; the pair sits in different themes so it is not mere shared-hierarchy overlap. Shared token overlap ('numbers', boilerplate 'pupils should be able to') alone is discounted.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Three Performance Objectives within the same Fractions topic (Theme: Number and Numeration; Sub-Theme: Fraction). The first objective, stating the fraction of a group of concrete objects, establishes foundational recognition and naming of fractions; the second, using the symbols < or > to order fractions, presupposes the ability to identify and represent fractions in order to compare and order them. Proficiency in identifying/stating fractions substantively supports success in ordering them, so the developmental direction runs first_to_second. Same-rank (Primary Three) direction is justified by this conceptual dependency rather than by shared hierarchy or numbering alone.

judgment.rationale: Both are PRIMARY ONE Performance Objectives under the same Topic '1. Money' (Sub-Theme Primary Measures). The first is 'add coins to obtain sums not exceeding 25k' (arithmetic with money) and the second is 'trace coins using brown and white papers' (a manipulative/recognition activity for coins). They share substantive coherence around coins/money and reinforce each other within the same topic, but neither is a clear developmental precursor of the other: tracing coins is a hands-on familiarization/art task while adding coins is numeric computation, and both sit at the same grade rank (0). Coin/money coherence supports relatesTo; there is no evidence of a directed buildsTowards dependency, so a symmetric relation is appropriate.
